newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal says slight tax shortfall unimportant.
newsitem.headline: Portugal says slight tax shortfall unimportant.

text.p: Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday that Portugal would make its 1997 budget deficit goal despite a slight shortfall in tax receipts in the first half.
"Tax receipts are performing normally...we will have the deficit as forecast," he told Reuters.

Earlier, the ministry announced that tax receipts grew 8.8 percent year-on-year in the first six months of 1997 against the 8.9 percent written into the budget with its deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"You can say that the first half was slightly less good than would be desirable but it does not jeopardise the (deficit) programme for the end of the year," he said.

Sousa Franco, who spoke to Reuters before addressing the American Club of Lisbon, said the main cause of the shortfall was the fact that the government had not adjusted petroleum tax upwards after international oil prices declined.
"This cost us 19.5 billion escudos up to the end of June," he said. "This is the only significant cause (of the shortfall)," he said.
